bb.name: Regional Manager
bb.description: Experimental: it may break with a bb update. Start a regional manager: a long-lived thread that takes on a body of work, plans it as issues, and starts an agent, a child thread, on each issue; all of one manager's agents are its crew. Open its panel in the navigation rail and press New: give it a name, an optional description and an avatar, a still blob in one of 21 shapes and 11 colours, and press Create, which saves it with no thread and opens its page; there bb's own new-thread composer, already set to a fresh worktree and auto permissions, takes its goal, and sending it starts the manager's thread, titled with the name, on what the composer picked, the goal its first message and its GOAL.md. The panel lists each manager by its avatar, its name and its description, the ones not started yet under Not started and the others under their project; a row opens a started manager's thread, and the page of one not started yet, which edits all three, deletes it, and names it in bb's title bar. Above a started manager's composer, its avatar and name open the same editor below them, while a rename in bb's sidebar renames it too and never changes its avatar. It keeps the work in its issues, what was decided about each included, and its notes and your standing rules for it in a folder of markdown files on the bb server. It writes to you answer first and in proportion to the question, and stays quiet on a wake that brings you nothing to know or decide. Each issue is numbered after a key taken from its project's name, as BBP-4 in bb-plugins, and is build work, code verified on its own branch, or research, a probe, spike, investigation or design whose result is a report; it has a description for you, a brief and done-criteria for its agent (for research, the questions its report answers), and a status the plugin derives from what its agents did: Backlog, Todo, In progress, Reviewing, Verifying, In review, Done or Canceled, with Needs you flagged above them when only you can act. An issue can depend on others: it is blocked while one of them is open, derived on every read and never stored, and a dependency that would close a cycle is refused; dependencies inform and never refuse, so the manager can start an agent on a blocked issue, its catch-up lists the issues ready to start, and it is woken when a merge or a handoff unblocks one, while a dependency carries nothing between issues. An issue can be split into sub-issues, one level deep: the parent never has an agent, its status rolls up from theirs, and its dependencies block them; once all of a build parent's work is merged, an independent verifier the plugin starts checks its own done-criteria on the default branch, a final check that makes it Done, while a failed one is the manager's to fix with a new sub-issue. An agent works on its own branch, in a fresh worktree or a sandbox, on the provider and model the manager names or else on the manager's own; when the manager hands an issue to a new agent, the old one is stopped, never archived, and the new one continues in its environment, on its branch with its uncommitted files and pull request, moves the work to a new environment on a branch cut from its branch (through origin, once pushed, when a sandbox is on either side), or starts clean from the default branch, with every earlier handoff and verdict in its first message; the manager also names what verifies each build issue, from the preferences you give it, and the plugin picks an independent verifier when it names none. An agent ends its work with one handoff (done, blocked or gave up, with what it did and its evidence), stored whole. A research agent's done handoff carries its report: nothing verifies it, the issue is Done at once, and the plugin saves the report as a file in the manager's memory, which the manager names in the briefs of the agents that need it; the plugin hands it to nobody. Every done handoff of build work is first reviewed by a reviewer the plugin starts itself, a hidden thread in the agent's environment on a model other than the agent's and the verifier's when bb has one, which reviews the diff as the manager's CREW.md instructs reviewers (the plugin names no review of its own) and reports findings, each with a file, line, severity and claim, while the issue is Reviewing; a reviewer that can't start, stalls or stops without reporting never holds the issue. Then it is checked by a verifier the plugin starts itself: a hidden thread in the agent's environment, on another model than the agent's when bb has one, that runs what proves each done-criterion, triages each of the reviewer's findings with a reason, with anything it asks a person declined, and returns a verdict with the output as evidence, while the plugin itself checks that the claimed commit is checked out on a clean tree. The reviewer and the verifier get the issue's decisions, and work that follows one is never a finding. A must-fix fails the verdict, as a failed criterion does, only when the verifier anchors it: a bug hit in normal use, with the steps that reach it, or a broken done-criterion, requirement the brief states explicitly or recorded decision; it downgrades one that meets none, as a principle or REVIEW.md violation or a bug that needs a contrived setup, and should-fix and nit findings never fail it. A verdict that passed waits for CI when the issue has a pull request. An agent's first failed verdict goes straight back to it as the verifier's message, with only the anchored must-fixes and a count of the other findings that held; a second goes to the manager, which sees every finding with the verifier's triage and reason. When an issue passes with a confirmed should-fix or a downgraded must-fix left, the plugin files every finding its rounds held without blocking it as one follow-up, a top-level build issue in Backlog that stays blocked until the issue is Done, named in the issue's Activity and the manager's update; nits alone file nothing and stay in the feed. An issue gets 3 failed verdicts across all its agents: at the third, and each later one you haven't allowed, nothing goes back to any agent and the plugin itself asks you on the board, leading with why the last round failed; until you answer, the manager can't start or message an agent on it, any answer allows one more round, and the question leaves Needs you once the issue closes. The plugin wakes the manager with a short message, hidden from you, that names what happened and never quotes an agent: on handoffs, final checks, failures, an agent waiting on you, an issue back in Todo or unblocked, pull request and CI changes read through gh, your comments on issues, memory edits, answers and verification switch, and its own reminders. When only you can decide something, it puts a question with up to five options on its board and keeps working; a question about an issue keeps your answer among that issue's decisions, beside those the manager records on it, and every agent started on it gets them. Its Board, a tab in its thread's side panel, shows the verification switch, its open decisions and every issue in a folding lane per status, each with its pull request and CI, what blocks it and what it blocks, and a card on hover with its headline, sub-issues hung under their parent, each opening in its own tab beside the Board, or focusing the one it has, to what it is about, its parent and sub-issues, what it depends on and blocks, its criteria as a grid of each round's result, and its Activity, filtered to All, Rounds or Discussion: every round, a handoff or a build parent's final check with its review and verdict, folded to its score with the latest open, among the decisions, questions and comments about it, an open question's options answering it there, each moment with the status it moved the issue to, and quiet lines for its agents, pull request, CI and the manager's changes to its plan, from where the record began for an issue filed before it was kept, and at its foot a field whose every comment goes to the manager, which replies on the issue, records a decision or, when it concerns the agent's work and no check is running, relays it to the agent, who can reply there too; it reads again only when its own issue changes. Issue links in chat are experimental, and the likeliest part to break with a bb update: the manager names an issue to you as a link, which reads as the issue's live status glyph and its id, mid-sentence, shows its card from the Board on hover or focus, and when pressed opens its tab beside the Board, from any other thread in a split; without the plugin it is a plain link reading as the id. The board warns when the manager edits files in its own environment. Below it, Memory, a section that folds like a lane and stays folded through a reload, shows the manager's memory files as one row of cards that scrolls sideways, each previewing its file, named under it with its folder, and opens one to read and edit in place, never letting you and the thread silently overwrite each other.
